page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-8 is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs, which map to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports hardware-level features such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX), AES and VAES cryptography, SHA_NI, and hypervisor virtualization. This configuration does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the c2d-standard-8 delivers strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of tested servers with a stress-ng single-core score of 2865.09. Multi-core CPU performance falls within the average range, yielding a stress-ng multi-core score of 11559.23. Memory bandwidth is also average, measuring 553.27 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 46.79 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Other average-tier results include a Geekbench single-core score of 1658.0, a multi-core score of 6531.0, and a static web serving throughput of 10.68 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated AMD EPYC cores offer a reliable performance-per-resource profile for compute-bound tasks without the overhead of GPU hardware or local NVMe storage. The lack of local storage requires external block storage attachment, which represents a key architectural tradeoff. This server is suited for general-purpose compute workloads, software compilation, static web serving, and moderate database operations.
